One joint probe against a clean probe.py BASELINE (real 306, T419/O421, multiset 30t): emptying the guard body while making its operand a volatile read moved the count from +2 LONG to -2 SHORT (O421 -> O417) and worsened the multiset 30t -> 32t, with `real` unchanged at 306. The aligned view (fnasm --diff 0x5c0:0x5f4) is the evidence: the target's `mulli r0,r21,12` + `lfsx f1,r22,r0` pair BELOW the guard collapsed in our build to a single `lfs f1,3092(r29)`, and the volatile load reappeared at 0x5dc, below the fold, instead of at the compare.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
EMPTYING A GUARD BODY IS NOT A LOCAL EDIT: IT PROPAGATES DOWNSTREAM. claim.law.IT_empty-bodied-if-elides-its-own-comparison.20260901.v1 correctly says MWCC's front end discards a syntactically empty conditional body whole, comparison and operand loads included. What that law does not say, and what is measured here, is that the elision also removes the last WRITE to the guarded variable, which unblocks constant propagation of that variable into every use BELOW the guard. Where the guarded variable indexes an array further down, the target's `mulli` + indexed `lfsx`/`lwzx` access folds to a plain displacement load, and you lose two instructions of correct downstream STRUCTURE while trying to remove one surplus branch. Budget the probe accordingly: an empty-body probe on a variable with downstream uses can remove MORE instructions than the surplus you were targeting -- here 4 removed where 2 were surplus, overshooting a +2 count gap into -2 -- so read the whole function's --ops after the probe, never just the cluster you edited.

VOLATILE DOES NOT RESCUE IT, AND THIS BOUNDS THE DEAD-STORE LEVER. The obvious counter-form is to qualify the compared operand volatile so the guard cannot be optimised away, per claim.law.SI_dead-store-body-strands-the-compare-when-operands-are-volatile.20260901.v1. Measured jointly with the empty body, that fails in an instructive way: the volatile LOAD is emitted, as the qualifier requires, but MWCC SINKS it past the constant fold to a position where nothing consumes it, and NO comparison is emitted at all. So `volatile` anchors the load and only the load; it does not anchor the comparison that consumes it. Any lever whose goal is a STRANDED COMPARE -- a `cmpwi` the target keeps with no branch and no body -- therefore cannot be built out of `volatile` plus an empty body, and the dead-store law's applicability is correspondingly narrower than its statement suggests: it needs the compared VALUE to be unknown to the optimizer, which a volatile-qualified read of a global does not make it, because the folding happens on the OTHER operand (your own constant-initialised local).

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR SCREENING. These two laws read as complements and invite exactly the joint probe AGENTS residual-work discipline 6 makes mandatory when two separately-parked axes touch the same instructions. That joint probe is worth running -- it is how this mechanism was found -- but expect it to be NEGATIVE wherever the guarded variable has downstream index uses, and screen for those uses BEFORE spending the build. Cheap pre-screen: grep the variable's remaining uses after the guard; if any of them multiplies or indexes with it, the empty-body family is closed at that site without a probe.

METRIC WARNING, INDEPENDENTLY USEFUL. probe.py returned the verdict NEUTRAL for this probe because `real` was unchanged at 306, while the instruction count moved 421 -> 417 and the multiset moved 30t -> 32t. A NEUTRAL verdict is NOT evidence that a probe was inert; read the count and multiset off the same run before believing it, and note that a NEUTRAL state is BANKED as probe.py's revert point, so `--revert` will refuse to undo it and the edit must be restored by hand.
